title: Permission Without a Schedule
reflection:
You used to know roughly which days would ask you to stop. Now the asking comes without warning — a heaviness that arrives on no calendar, demanding the same permission all the same.

You may stop today, unscheduled as it is. The permission doesn't expire just because you can't predict when you'll need it next.
closing: I receive permission to stop, even without a schedule to justify it. It is given anyway. Amen.

scripture.text: Come to me, all who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

title: A Sabbath With No Fixed Day
reflection:
The Sabbath was written into the structure of things, one day in seven, easy to plan around. Your body's sabbath now arrives less predictably — but it is no less written in, no less owed.

When the need for rest comes, however irregular its timing, give your body what it's owed.
closing: My rest is not laziness, even on an unpredictable schedule. It is obedience to a rhythm still older than the calendar. Amen.

scripture.text: Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.

title: Strength, Unscheduled
reflection:
Rested strength doesn't always return on the timetable you expect. Some days it simply arrives — earlier or later than you'd have guessed, real all the same.

Receive it without needing it to explain its timing. Use it gently.
closing: Thank you for this unscheduled strength. Let me use it without demanding it promise to stay. Amen.

scripture.text: He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might he increases strength.

title: Resting in the Not-Knowing
reflection:
Rest is harder to plan when you don't know which kind of day is coming. But surrender was never really about knowing in advance — only about yielding to what actually arrives.

Let today's not-knowing be itself a place to rest, rather than a problem to solve before you're allowed to.
closing: I yield to this not-knowing the way I'd yield to gravity. Let the ground hold me even here. Amen.

scripture.text: Not my will, but yours be done.
